answer.origin: Fox News Digital article by Amanda Macias, published 2026-07-01, based on interviews with Corning Chairman, CEO and President Wendell Weeks, Corning planning supervisor Emily Capek, and Wistron Chairman Simon Lin. Fox News attributes the NVIDIA-Corning facility and Wistron details to its own reporting; no NVIDIA company statement is quoted.
answer.note: Covered company is NVIDIA (NVDA); the source is a Corning-centred feature, so Corning's own growth claims are not NVIDIA facts. The NVIDIA-relevant content is that, per Fox News reporting dated 2026-07-01, NVIDIA partnered with Corning earlier in 2026 to build three advanced optical manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas, expected to create more than 3,000 jobs and expand Corning's U.S. optical manufacturing capacity tenfold. This is a reported partnership and a forecast, not a completed project. It supports a conditional lead that NVIDIA's AI-system build-out relies on U.S. optical-fiber supply that Corning is scaling, with the fiber connecting AI systems described as a supply input rather than a confirmed NVIDIA purchase volume. Separately, Fox News reports that Taiwan-based Wistron is establishing AI-supercomputer manufacturing in Texas for NVIDIA, a U.S. manufacturing-footprint lead with no disclosed headcount, capacity, investment amount or start date. Weeks' statement that Corning will probably double in size over coming years, with almost all new hires in advanced manufacturing, is a hedged party forecast about Corning and does not quantify NVIDIA-linked volume. Capek's comment that demand for AI platforms is driving need for Corning fiber is a plant-level qualitative statement.
limitations: No NVIDIA-side statement, filing, or press release is cited; the partnership is known only through Fox News reporting and Corning-side quotes.

The Corning-NVIDIA partnership terms are not disclosed: no offtake, purchase commitment, prepayment, equity, capacity-reservation, or cost-sharing terms are identified, so NVIDIA's contractual obligation is unknown.
The 3,000-job and tenfold-capacity figures are described as expected and carry no completion date, measurement period, or definition of the baseline for the tenfold claim.
Corning's 'double our size' remark has no stated timeframe ('over the coming years') and is not tied to NVIDIA revenue or volume.
The Wistron Texas operation has no disclosed job count, capacity, investment, or start date, and its scope for NVIDIA is limited to the source's wording.
The source does not say how much of Corning's optical-fiber output goes to NVIDIA-linked AI infrastructure versus other customers.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's newsroom, 8-K filings, and latest annual/quarterly reports for any Corning partnership, investment, or supply agreement and its disclosed terms.
Check Corning's latest 10-Q/10-K and earnings materials for the named NVIDIA facilities, expected completion dates, capacity figures, and any customer concentration disclosure.
Check Wistron's public filings, Texas economic-development announcements, and NVIDIA statements for the Texas AI-supercomputer facility's headcount, capex, and start date.
Check whether the 3,000-job and tenfold-capacity figures appear in an official Corning or NVIDIA release and whether the basis of the tenfold comparison is stated.
